headline: High-risk shared git workspace and shell/write overlap can cause prompt injection, data leakage, and destructive conflicts between Aider and Superset.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can execute shell commands, while Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. A shared repo or exported content could let attacker-controlled text from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is plausible, but not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents exchange content through a shared repository or exported files
IF either agent parses the other's file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text
Add provenance tags to exchanged files
Review any cross-agent file before use
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the handoff boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can read/write the filesystem; Superset has API access and allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or history can flow into outputs or API-backed context. The profiles do not show direct secret handling by Superset, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or mounted workspace
IF Superset ingests files or query text originating from Aider
mitigations: Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive samples

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and git-state modification; Superset can call APIs and has network egress. In a shared repo or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes and state changes can collide and corrupt work. Because Aider explicitly auto-commits to git and no locking is shown for either agent, high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, repo, or mutable API-backed resource
IF no external lock or transaction coordinator is present
mitigations: Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use file locks or git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can produce code changes and git commits, and Superset can consume API inputs and act as a data-engineering system. If Superset treats Aider's outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream analytics or operational actions. The profiles do not prove automatic action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Aider-generated files, SQL, or config without validation
IF downstream jobs or dashboards rely on those inputs
mitigations: Validate schemas and SQL before execution
Compare outputs against a second source
Limit Aider changes to non-production branches

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code, git history, and model-provider API keys, while Superset's profile shows no touched data classes or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance concern is potential handling of secrets in Aider; the pair does not show a documented residency or certification mismatch, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF Aider is used on repositories containing regulated secrets or personal data
IF Superset is configured to ingest that regulated data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared repos
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
